O.outcome_detail: acceptance-scale model fit and dimensional representation

result.effect: bifactor CFI=.979, RMSEA=.069; one-factor CFI=.895, RMSEA=.137

cells.quote: The one-factor model fitted poorly [χ2(65) = 555.1; RMSEA = .137, 90% CI [.127, .148]; CFI = .895; SRMR = .054], so a strictly unidimensional first-order representation is inadequate despite the parallel-analysis result. The four-factor, second-order, and bifactor models all fitted well, the bifactor model best [χ2(52) = 151.9; CFI = .979; TLI = .968; RMSEA = .069 [.057, .082]; SRMR = .023].
cells.note: The contrast concerns competing measurement models, not an instructional treatment.

result.effect: ECV=.822; ωh=.927; PUC=.808; HTMT up to .94

cells.quote: A bifactor analysis showed a dominant general factor (ECV = .82; ωh = .93; PUC = .81), and the bifactor model was not identifiable under WLSMV, consistent with very weak specific factors (although non-identification can also reflect model instability).
cells.note: The general factor is supported for scoring, while the subdimensions lack discriminant validity; the direction is coded as favoring general-factor scoring.

result.effect: S-1: χ2(55)=193.4; CFI=.992; TLI=.989; RMSEA=.079; SRMR=.022; full model non-identified

cells.quote: The bifactor model could not be identified under WLSMV (its information matrix was non-invertible); this is consistent with specific factors carrying too little variance to be reliably estimated, although non-identification can also reflect model instability or over-parameterization, so it is read cautiously rather than as confirmation. To probe the source of the non-identification, an S-1 bifactor model (Eid et al., 2017) omitting the weakest specific factor (effectiveness; ML specific loadings .06–.46) was estimated under WLSMV. This model converged and was identified, with good fit [χ2(55) = 193.4; CFI = .992; TLI = .989; RMSEA = .079; SRMR = .022] and substantial general-factor loadings (.68–.94).
cells.note: Convergence of the S-1 diagnostic implicates the effectiveness-specific factor but does not establish it as the sole source of non-identification.
